29: // Parse parses the input just enough to group tokens, in
30: // order, by server block. No further parsing is performed.
31: // Server blocks are returned in the order in which they appear.
32: // Directives that do not appear in validDirectives will cause
33: // an error. If you do not want to check for valid directives,
34: // pass in nil instead.

36: // Environment variables in {$ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE} notation
37: // will be replaced before parsing begins.
38: func Parse(filename string, input []byte) ([]ServerBlock, error) {
39: 	// unfortunately, we must copy the input because parsing must
40: 	// remain a read-only operation, but we have to expand environment
41: 	// variables before we parse, which changes the underlying array (#4422)
42: 	inputCopy := make([]byte, len(input))
43: 	copy(inputCopy, input)
44: 
45: 	tokens, err := allTokens(filename, inputCopy)
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return nil, err
48: 	}
49: 	p := parser{
50: 		Dispenser: NewDispenser(tokens),
51: 		importGraph: importGraph{
52: 			nodes: make(map[string]bool),
53: 			edges: make(adjacency),
54: 		},
55: 	}
56: 	return p.parseAll()
57: }

59: // allTokens lexes the entire input, but does not parse it.
60: // It returns all the tokens from the input, unstructured
61: // and in order. It may mutate input as it expands env vars.
62: func allTokens(filename string, input []byte) ([]Token, error) {
63: 	return Tokenize(replaceEnvVars(input), filename)
64: }

66: // replaceEnvVars replaces all occurrences of environment variables.
67: // It mutates the underlying array and returns the updated slice.
68: func replaceEnvVars(input []byte) []byte {
69: 	var offset int
70: 	for {
71: 		begin := bytes.Index(input[offset:], spanOpen)
72: 		if begin < 0 {
73: 			break
74: 		}
75: 		begin += offset // make beginning relative to input, not offset
76: 		end := bytes.Index(input[begin+len(spanOpen):], spanClose)
77: 		if end < 0 {
78: 			break
79: 		}
80: 		end += begin + len(spanOpen) // make end relative to input, not begin
81: 
82: 		// get the name; if there is no name, skip it
83: 		envString := input[begin+len(spanOpen) : end]
84: 		if len(envString) == 0 {
85: 			offset = end + len(spanClose)
86: 			continue
87: 		}
88: 
89: 		// split the string into a key and an optional default
90: 		envParts := strings.SplitN(string(envString), envVarDefaultDelimiter, 2)
91: 
92: 		// do a lookup for the env var, replace with the default if not found
93: 		envVarValue, found := os.LookupEnv(envParts[0])
94: 		if !found && len(envParts) == 2 {
95: 			envVarValue = envParts[1]
96: 		}
97: 
98: 		// get the value of the environment variable
99: 		// note that this causes one-level deep chaining
100: 		envVarBytes := []byte(envVarValue)
101: 
102: 		// splice in the value
103: 		input = append(input[:begin],
104: 			append(envVarBytes, input[end+len(spanClose):]...)...)
105: 
106: 		// continue at the end of the replacement
107: 		offset = begin + len(envVarBytes)
108: 	}
109: 	return input
110: }

125: 		err := p.parseOne()

127: 			return blocks, err

129: 		if len(p.block.Keys) > 0 || len(p.block.Segments) > 0 {
130: 			blocks = append(blocks, p.block)

145: func (p *parser) begin() error {
146: 	if len(p.tokens) == 0 {
147: 		return nil
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	err := p.addresses()
151: 	if err != nil {
152: 		return err
153: 	}
154: 
155: 	if p.eof {
156: 		// this happens if the Caddyfile consists of only
157: 		// a line of addresses and nothing else
158: 		return nil
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	if ok, name := p.isNamedRoute(); ok {
162: 		// named routes only have one key, the route name
163: 		p.block.Keys = []string{name}
164: 		p.block.IsNamedRoute = true
165: 
166: 		// we just need a dummy leading token to ease parsing later
167: 		nameToken := p.Token()
168: 		nameToken.Text = name
169: 
170: 		// get all the tokens from the block, including the braces
171: 		tokens, err := p.blockTokens(true)
172: 		if err != nil {
173: 			return err
174: 		}
175: 		tokens = append([]Token{nameToken}, tokens...)
176: 		p.block.Segments = []Segment{tokens}
177: 		return nil
178: 	}
179: 
180: 	if ok, name := p.isSnippet(); ok {
181: 		if p.definedSnippets == nil {
182: 			p.definedSnippets = map[string][]Token{}
183: 		}
184: 		if _, found := p.definedSnippets[name]; found {
185: 			return p.Errf("redeclaration of previously declared snippet %s", name)
186: 		}
187: 		// consume all tokens til matched close brace
188: 		tokens, err := p.blockTokens(false)
189: 		if err != nil {
190: 			return err
191: 		}
192: 		// Just as we need to track which file the token comes from, we need to
193: 		// keep track of which snippet the token comes from. This is helpful
194: 		// in tracking import cycles across files/snippets by namespacing them.
195: 		// Without this, we end up with false-positives in cycle-detection.
196: 		for k, v := range tokens {
197: 			v.snippetName = name
198: 			tokens[k] = v
199: 		}
200: 		p.definedSnippets[name] = tokens
201: 		// empty block keys so we don't save this block as a real server.
202: 		p.block.Keys = nil
203: 		return nil
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	return p.blockContents()
207: }

209: func (p *parser) addresses() error {
210: 	var expectingAnother bool
211: 
212: 	for {
213: 		tkn := p.Val()
214: 
215: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
216: 		if tkn == "import" && p.isNewLine() {
217: 			err := p.doImport(0)
218: 			if err != nil {
219: 				return err
220: 			}
221: 			continue
222: 		}
223: 
224: 		// Open brace definitely indicates end of addresses
225: 		if tkn == "{" {
226: 			if expectingAnother {
227: 				return p.Errf("Expected another address but had '%s' - check for extra comma", tkn)
228: 			}
229: 			// Mark this server block as being defined with braces.
230: 			// This is used to provide a better error message when
231: 			// the user may have tried to define two server blocks
232: 			// without having used braces, which are required in
233: 			// that case.
234: 			p.block.HasBraces = true
235: 			break
236: 		}
237: 
238: 		// Users commonly forget to place a space between the address and the '{'
239: 		if strings.HasSuffix(tkn, "{") {
240: 			return p.Errf("Site addresses cannot end with a curly brace: '%s' - put a space between the token and the brace", tkn)
241: 		}
242: 
243: 		if tkn != "" { // empty token possible if user typed ""
244: 			// Trailing comma indicates another address will follow, which
245: 			// may possibly be on the next line
246: 			if tkn[len(tkn)-1] == ',' {
247: 				tkn = tkn[:len(tkn)-1]
248: 				expectingAnother = true
249: 			} else {
250: 				expectingAnother = false // but we may still see another one on this line
251: 			}
252: 
253: 			// If there's a comma here, it's probably because they didn't use a space
254: 			// between their two domains, e.g. "foo.com,bar.com", which would not be
255: 			// parsed as two separate site addresses.
256: 			if strings.Contains(tkn, ",") {
257: 				return p.Errf("Site addresses cannot contain a comma ',': '%s' - put a space after the comma to separate site addresses", tkn)
258: 			}
259: 
260: 			p.block.Keys = append(p.block.Keys, tkn)
261: 		}
262: 
263: 		// Advance token and possibly break out of loop or return error
264: 		hasNext := p.Next()
265: 		if expectingAnother && !hasNext {
266: 			return p.EOFErr()
267: 		}
268: 		if !hasNext {
269: 			p.eof = true
270: 			break // EOF
271: 		}
272: 		if !expectingAnother && p.isNewLine() {
273: 			break
274: 		}
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	return nil
278: }

280: func (p *parser) blockContents() error {
281: 	errOpenCurlyBrace := p.openCurlyBrace()
282: 	if errOpenCurlyBrace != nil {
283: 		// single-server configs don't need curly braces
284: 		p.cursor--
285: 	}
286: 
287: 	err := p.directives()
288: 	if err != nil {
289: 		return err
290: 	}
291: 
292: 	// only look for close curly brace if there was an opening
293: 	if errOpenCurlyBrace == nil {
294: 		err = p.closeCurlyBrace()
295: 		if err != nil {
296: 			return err
297: 		}
298: 	}
299: 
300: 	return nil
301: }

303: // directives parses through all the lines for directives
304: // and it expects the next token to be the first
305: // directive. It goes until EOF or closing curly brace
306: // which ends the server block.
307: func (p *parser) directives() error {
308: 	for p.Next() {
309: 		// end of server block
310: 		if p.Val() == "}" {
311: 			// p.nesting has already been decremented
312: 			break
313: 		}
314: 
315: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
316: 		if p.Val() == "import" {
317: 			err := p.doImport(1)
318: 			if err != nil {
319: 				return err
320: 			}
321: 			p.cursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
322: 			continue
323: 		}
324: 
325: 		// normal case: parse a directive as a new segment
326: 		// (a "segment" is a line which starts with a directive
327: 		// and which ends at the end of the line or at the end of
328: 		// the block that is opened at the end of the line)
329: 		if err := p.directive(); err != nil {
330: 			return err
331: 		}
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	return nil
335: }

337: // doImport swaps out the import directive and its argument
338: // (a total of 2 tokens) with the tokens in the specified file
339: // or globbing pattern. When the function returns, the cursor
340: // is on the token before where the import directive was. In
341: // other words, call Next() to access the first token that was
342: // imported.
343: func (p *parser) doImport(nesting int) error {
344: 	// syntax checks
345: 	if !p.NextArg() {
346: 		return p.ArgErr()
347: 	}
348: 	importPattern := p.Val()
349: 	if importPattern == "" {
350: 		return p.Err("Import requires a non-empty filepath")
351: 	}
352: 
353: 	// grab remaining args as placeholder replacements
354: 	args := p.RemainingArgs()
355: 
356: 	// set up a replacer for non-variadic args replacement
357: 	repl := makeArgsReplacer(args)
358: 
359: 	// splice out the import directive and its arguments
360: 	// (2 tokens, plus the length of args)
361: 	tokensBefore := p.tokens[:p.cursor-1-len(args)]
362: 	tokensAfter := p.tokens[p.cursor+1:]
363: 	var importedTokens []Token
364: 	var nodes []string
365: 
366: 	// first check snippets. That is a simple, non-recursive replacement
367: 	if p.definedSnippets != nil && p.definedSnippets[importPattern] != nil {
368: 		importedTokens = p.definedSnippets[importPattern]
369: 		if len(importedTokens) > 0 {
370: 			// just grab the first one
371: 			nodes = append(nodes, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", importedTokens[0].File, importedTokens[0].snippetName))
372: 		}
373: 	} else {
374: 		// make path relative to the file of the _token_ being processed rather
375: 		// than current working directory (issue #867) and then use glob to get
376: 		// list of matching filenames
377: 		absFile, err := filepath.Abs(p.Dispenser.File())
378: 		if err != nil {
379: 			return p.Errf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", p.Dispenser.File(), err)
380: 		}
381: 
382: 		var matches []string
383: 		var globPattern string
384: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(importPattern) {
385: 			globPattern = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(absFile), importPattern)
386: 		} else {
387: 			globPattern = importPattern
388: 		}
389: 		if strings.Count(globPattern, "*") > 1 || strings.Count(globPattern, "?") > 1 ||
390: 			(strings.Contains(globPattern, "[") && strings.Contains(globPattern, "]")) {
391: 			// See issue #2096 - a pattern with many glob expansions can hang for too long
392: 			return p.Errf("Glob pattern may only contain one wildcard (*), but has others: %s", globPattern)
393: 		}
394: 		matches, err = filepath.Glob(globPattern)
395: 
396: 		if err != nil {
397: 			return p.Errf("Failed to use import pattern %s: %v", importPattern, err)
398: 		}
399: 		if len(matches) == 0 {
400: 			if strings.ContainsAny(globPattern, "*?[]") {
401: 				caddy.Log().Warn("No files matching import glob pattern", zap.String("pattern", importPattern))
402: 			} else {
403: 				return p.Errf("File to import not found: %s", importPattern)
404: 			}
405: 		} else {
406: 			// See issue #5295 - should skip any files that start with a . when iterating over them.
407: 			sep := string(filepath.Separator)
408: 			segGlobPattern := strings.Split(globPattern, sep)
409: 			if strings.HasPrefix(segGlobPattern[len(segGlobPattern)-1], "*") {
410: 				var tmpMatches []string
411: 				for _, m := range matches {
412: 					seg := strings.Split(m, sep)
413: 					if !strings.HasPrefix(seg[len(seg)-1], ".") {
414: 						tmpMatches = append(tmpMatches, m)
415: 					}
416: 				}
417: 				matches = tmpMatches
418: 			}
419: 		}
420: 
421: 		// collect all the imported tokens
422: 		for _, importFile := range matches {
423: 			newTokens, err := p.doSingleImport(importFile)
424: 			if err != nil {
425: 				return err
426: 			}
427: 			importedTokens = append(importedTokens, newTokens...)
428: 		}
429: 		nodes = matches
430: 	}
431: 
432: 	nodeName := p.File()
433: 	if p.Token().snippetName != "" {
434: 		nodeName += fmt.Sprintf(":%s", p.Token().snippetName)
435: 	}
436: 	p.importGraph.addNode(nodeName)
437: 	p.importGraph.addNodes(nodes)
438: 	if err := p.importGraph.addEdges(nodeName, nodes); err != nil {
439: 		p.importGraph.removeNodes(nodes)
440: 		return err
441: 	}
442: 
443: 	// copy the tokens so we don't overwrite p.definedSnippets
444: 	tokensCopy := make([]Token, 0, len(importedTokens))
445: 
446: 	var (
447: 		maybeSnippet   bool
448: 		maybeSnippetId bool
449: 		index          int
450: 	)
451: 
452: 	// run the argument replacer on the tokens
453: 	// golang for range slice return a copy of value
454: 	// similarly, append also copy value
455: 	for i, token := range importedTokens {
456: 		// update the token's imports to refer to import directive filename, line number and snippet name if there is one
457: 		if token.snippetName != "" {
458: 			token.imports = append(token.imports, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d (import %s)", p.File(), p.Line(), token.snippetName))
459: 		} else {
460: 			token.imports = append(token.imports, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d (import)", p.File(), p.Line()))
461: 		}
462: 
463: 		// naive way of determine snippets, as snippets definition can only follow name + block
464: 		// format, won't check for nesting correctness or any other error, that's what parser does.
465: 		if !maybeSnippet && nesting == 0 {
466: 			// first of the line
467: 			if i == 0 || importedTokens[i-1].File != token.File || importedTokens[i-1].Line+importedTokens[i-1].NumLineBreaks() < token.Line {
468: 				index = 0
469: 			} else {
470: 				index++
471: 			}
472: 
473: 			if index == 0 && len(token.Text) >= 3 && strings.HasPrefix(token.Text, "(") && strings.HasSuffix(token.Text, ")") {
474: 				maybeSnippetId = true
475: 			}
476: 		}
477: 
478: 		switch token.Text {
479: 		case "{":
480: 			nesting++
481: 			if index == 1 && maybeSnippetId && nesting == 1 {
482: 				maybeSnippet = true
483: 				maybeSnippetId = false
484: 			}
485: 		case "}":
486: 			nesting--
487: 			if nesting == 0 && maybeSnippet {
488: 				maybeSnippet = false
489: 			}
490: 		}
491: 
492: 		if maybeSnippet {
493: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
494: 			continue
495: 		}
496: 
497: 		foundVariadic, startIndex, endIndex := parseVariadic(token, len(args))
498: 		if foundVariadic {
499: 			for _, arg := range args[startIndex:endIndex] {
500: 				token.Text = arg
501: 				tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
502: 			}
503: 		} else {
504: 			token.Text = repl.ReplaceKnown(token.Text, "")
505: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
506: 		}
507: 	}
508: 
509: 	// splice the imported tokens in the place of the import statement
510: 	// and rewind cursor so Next() will land on first imported token
511: 	p.tokens = append(tokensBefore, append(tokensCopy, tokensAfter...)...)
512: 	p.cursor -= len(args) + 1
513: 
514: 	return nil
515: }

517: // doSingleImport lexes the individual file at importFile and returns
518: // its tokens or an error, if any.
519: func (p *parser) doSingleImport(importFile string) ([]Token, error) {
520: 	file, err := os.Open(importFile)
521: 	if err != nil {
522: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
523: 	}
524: 	defer file.Close()
525: 
526: 	if info, err := file.Stat(); err != nil {
527: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
528: 	} else if info.IsDir() {
529: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: is a directory", importFile)
530: 	}
531: 
532: 	input, err := io.ReadAll(file)
533: 	if err != nil {
534: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not read imported file %s: %v", importFile, err)
535: 	}
536: 
537: 	// only warning in case of empty files
538: 	if len(input) == 0 || len(strings.TrimSpace(string(input))) == 0 {
539: 		caddy.Log().Warn("Import file is empty", zap.String("file", importFile))
540: 		return []Token{}, nil
541: 	}
542: 
543: 	importedTokens, err := allTokens(importFile, input)
544: 	if err != nil {
545: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not read tokens while importing %s: %v", importFile, err)
546: 	}
547: 
548: 	// Tack the file path onto these tokens so errors show the imported file's name
549: 	// (we use full, absolute path to avoid bugs: issue #1892)
550: 	filename, err := filepath.Abs(importFile)
551: 	if err != nil {
552: 		return nil, p.Errf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", importFile, err)
553: 	}
554: 	for i := 0; i < len(importedTokens); i++ {
555: 		importedTokens[i].File = filename
556: 	}
557: 
558: 	return importedTokens, nil
559: }
